shipped_rows.title_o: Children learn spurious associations in their math textbooks: Examples from fraction arithmetic.

blind_target.authors: Tian, J., Braithwaite, D. W., & Siegler, R. S.
blind_target.title: Distributions of textbook tasks predict student learning: Data from decimal arithmetic.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
Our goal was to check whether Swiss

mathematics textbook series may also reveal imbalances in problem frequencies, as

reported by Braithwaite and Siegler (2018) and Tian et al. (2021) for U.S. textbooks.
blind_target.outcome_quote:
These patterns largely resemble, but differ also in part from those observed in U.S.

textbooks, analyzed by Braithwaite and Siegler (2018) and Tian et al. (2021). Most notably

(and to be explicitly tested in Study 2), in Swiss textbooks, children encounter +/- problems

involving fractions with unequal denominators more frequently than those involving equal

denominators. In contrast, U.S. textbooks present these two types of in roughly equal

proportions.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Study 1 confirms nonrandom decimal problem distributions but the authors also explicitly identify important distribution differences from the U.S. textbooks. The new child decimal tasks extend the finding rather than reproduce an original child experiment.

luna_triage.reason: Study 1 directly retests the specific published finding that U.S. textbook decimal problem distributions are imbalanced/nonrandom, by examining Swiss textbooks and comparing their patterns with Tian et al. (2021). The reference establishes the candidate as the primary empirical paper. The only supplied shipped original is row 456, Braithwaite and Siegler (2018), a separate fraction-arithmetic paper; the source itself distinguishes that work from Tian et al. (2021).
luna_triage.location: Introduction; Results, Section 2 (Textbook Content Analyses, Study 1), decimal results; Discussion; References.
luna_triage.omission_quote: A comparison of decimal problems in Swiss versus U.S. textbooks analysed by Tian et al. (2021) reveals important differences.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Tian, J., Braithwaite, D. W., & Siegler, R. S. (2021). Distributions of textbook tasks predict student learning: Data from decimal arithmetic. Journal of Educational Psychology, 113(3), 516–529. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000618
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: Tian, Braithwaite, and Siegler (2021) identified imbalanced distributions of decimal arithmetic problems in three U.S. mathematics textbook series to describe. Consistent with the results from Braithwaite and Siegler (2018) for fraction arithmetic, Tian et al. (2021) showed that these biased distributions influenced children’s decimal arithmetic by increasing the likelihood of learning spurious associations between operand features and operations.
